title: Explaining how
job: Steps and instructions in order, and what they are for
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE TU IMPERATIVE IS THE TU PRESENT WITH THE PRONOUN TAKEN OFF, AND AN -er VERB LOSES ITS -s AS WELL. tu regardes gives Regarde, tu écoutes gives Écoute, tu commences gives Commence. tu prends gives Prends and tu mets gives Mets, which keep theirs, because that -s is not an -er -s. aller is the exception inside the exception: Va, with the s coming back only in Vas-y.

THE POSITIVE ORDER TRANSFERS FREE AND THE NEGATIVE ONE DOES NOT. English puts don't in front and changes nothing else about the verb. French wraps it in two words: Ne commence pas, N'oublie pas. The ne is written every time, exactly as it has been since L1-M3, and speech dropping it changes nothing about what this course writes.

A PRONOUN GOES BEHIND A POSITIVE ORDER ON A HYPHEN, AND JUMPS BACK IN FRONT WHEN THE ORDER TURNS NEGATIVE. Mets-le becomes Ne le mets pas: the pronoun moves, and the hyphen disappears with the move. Behind the verb me also grows into moi, which is why it is Écoute-moi and never Écoute-me.

pour + INFINITIVE IS EXACTLY ENGLISH'S to ... . Appuie ici pour ouvrir la porte. The verb after pour never conjugates and never agrees with anybody, and pour itself is L2-M5's word doing the same job it always did. Nothing is being re-opened here; the infinitive behind it is the whole news.

il suffit de + INFINITIVE IS you just have to ... . It is a frozen frame with nobody in it, exactly like il faut: the il names no one, and whatever follows de stays an infinitive. English needs a person for this sentence and French refuses to supply one.

D'abord ... ensuite ... puis ... ORDERS THE STEPS, AND THEY ARE L2-M10'S AND L1-M10'S WORDS. Nothing new is opened by the ordering itself. What is new is that each slot now holds an ORDER rather than a statement, which is the whole difference between describing a routine and handing somebody one.

sentences.display: D'abord regarde la recette, ensuite coupe le pain
sentences.cue: First look at the recipe, then cut the bread
sentences.literal: First look the recipe, then cut the bread

words.note: The tu imperative of regarder: tu regardes with the pronoun gone and the -s gone with it. It takes no preposition — regarde la recette, never regarde à.
Feminine: la recette. Nothing to do with English receipt, which is un reçu — the two words split centuries ago and mean different things now.
Imperative of couper, an -er verb, so the -s goes: tu coupes gives Coupe. The final e is silent and the p in front of it is not.

sentences.trap: English looks AT the recipe; French looks it. regarder carries its object bare, so a regarde à la recette is the commonest first-week error, and it survives all the way into L4 if nobody names it.
sentences.sound: dah-BOR ruh-GARD la ruh-SET, ahn-SWEET koop luh PAN. The final e of regarde and of coupe is silent; the d and the p in front of them are heard.

variations.display: D'abord coupe le pain, ensuite ajoute le sel
variations.cue: First cut the bread, then add the salt
variations.changed: the same frame, two other steps in it

variations.display: Regarde la recette, puis coupe le pain
variations.cue: Look at the recipe, then cut the bread
variations.changed: d'abord and ensuite come off, and puis alone still orders the two

mistake.why: The -er imperative drops the -s: Regarde, not Regardes. That -s belongs to tu regardes, and tu is exactly what has gone.

sentences.usage: The opening line of any set of steps you hand to somebody you say tu to.
sentences.mnemonic: Take away tu, and take the -s with it.

sentences.display: Prends la casserole et mets l'eau sur le feu
sentences.cue: Take the pan and put the water on the heat
sentences.literal: Take the pan and put the-water on the fire

words.note: Imperative of prendre. Not an -er verb, so the -s STAYS: tu prends gives Prends. L2-M4 taught the infinitive; this is the order built from it.
Feminine: la casserole. It is a pan on a hob, not the baked dish English calls a casserole — that is un gratin.
Imperative of mettre, which is not an -er verb either, so its -s stays too: tu mets gives Mets. The -ts at the end is silent.

sentences.trap: Prends and Mets look like they ought to shed an -s the way Regarde does. They do not. Only -er verbs lose it, and prendre and mettre are not -er verbs.
sentences.sound: prahn la kas-ROL ay MEH loh sewr luh FUH. The -ds of prends and the -ts of mets are both silent, so both orders end on their vowel.

variations.display: Prends la casserole et mets le sel
variations.cue: Take the pan and put the salt in
variations.changed: the same pair of orders, with something else going in

variations.display: Mets l'eau sur le feu, puis prends la casserole
variations.cue: Put the water on the heat, then take the pan
variations.changed: the two orders swap, and nothing about their spelling moves

mistake.why: prendre keeps its -s in the tu imperative: Prends. Only -er verbs drop it.

sentences.usage: Step two of a recipe, said to somebody standing at the same worktop.

sentences.display: Ajoute le sel, puis attends cinq minutes
sentences.cue: Add the salt, then wait five minutes
sentences.literal: Add the salt, then wait five minutes

words.note: Imperative of ajouter, an -er verb: tu ajoutes gives Ajoute, with the -s gone. Adding TO something is ajouter à, but a bare object needs nothing.
Masculine: le sel. Le sel et le poivre is the pair, in the same order English says salt and pepper.
Imperative of attendre, L3-M5's verb: not an -er verb, so the -s stays. It takes no preposition — attends cinq minutes, never attends pour.
Feminine: une minute, cinq minutes. The plural -s is silent, so the singular and the plural sound identical.

sentences.trap: English waits FOR five minutes. French waits five minutes flat: attendre takes its object with no preposition at all, and the same is true of the person you are waiting for.
sentences.sound: a-ZHOOT luh SEL, pwee a-TAHN sank mee-NEWT. attends ends on a nasal vowel with nothing after it.

variations.display: Ajoute le sel, puis attends
variations.cue: Add the salt, then wait
variations.changed: the wait loses its length and the order still stands

variations.display: Coupe le pain, puis attends cinq minutes
variations.cue: Cut the bread, then wait five minutes
variations.changed: another first step in front of the same wait

mistake.why: ajouter is an -er verb, so its tu imperative drops the -s: Ajoute.

sentences.usage: The line that turns a list of ingredients into a set of steps.
sentences.mnemonic: French waits minutes, not for minutes.

sentences.display: Appuie ici pour ouvrir la porte
sentences.cue: Press here to open the door
sentences.literal: Press here for to-open the door

words.note: Imperative of appuyer, an -er verb, so no -s. You press ON a thing — appuie sur le bouton — but a place needs nothing: appuie ici.
The infinitive, because pour never takes a conjugated verb. ouvrir conjugates like an -er verb — tu ouvres — so its own order drops the -s the same way: Ouvre.
Feminine: la porte. Spelled exactly like the tu imperative of porter, to carry, so the sentence around it is what tells you which one you have.

sentences.trap: pour here is not a because and not English's for. Pour ouvrir is the PURPOSE of the pressing — to open — and a learner translating for opening lands on a shape French does not use.
sentences.sound: a-PWEE ee-SEE poor oo-VREER la PORT. appuie is two syllables, not three.

variations.display: Appuie ici pour ouvrir
variations.cue: Press here to open
variations.changed: the door drops off and the purpose stands alone

variations.display: Pour ouvrir la porte, appuie ici
variations.cue: To open the door, press here
variations.changed: the purpose leads and the order follows it

mistake.display: Appuie ici pour ouvres la porte
mistake.why: pour is always followed by the infinitive: pour ouvrir. Nothing after pour is ever conjugated.

sentences.usage: Written on machines and said at doors — the shape of every instruction that explains itself.
sentences.mnemonic: pour hands the next verb its infinitive.

sentences.display: Ne commence pas tout de suite, attends encore
sentences.cue: Don't start right away, wait a bit longer
sentences.literal: Not start not all of following, wait again

words.note: Imperative of commencer, an -er verb: no -s. Wrapped in ne ... pas here, and the verb itself does not change one letter for the negative.
One key, three words, said as one. It means immediately — a learner reaching for it to mean in a while has it exactly backwards.

sentences.trap: English negates an order with one word in front of it: don't start. French wraps the verb in two, ne ... pas, and the ne is never dropped in writing however freely speech drops it.
sentences.sound: nuh ko-MAHNS pah too duh SWEET, a-TAHN ahn-KOR. tout de suite runs together as one three-beat word.

variations.display: Ne coupe pas le pain tout de suite
variations.cue: Don't cut the bread right away
variations.changed: the same wrapper around another order

variations.display: Commence tout de suite
variations.cue: Start right away
variations.changed: the wrapper comes off and the order turns positive

mistake.why: Speech drops the ne; writing does not. Ne commence pas is what this course writes, every time.

sentences.usage: Said to somebody who has already picked up the knife.
sentences.mnemonic: ne in front, pas behind, the order in the middle.

sentences.display: Mets-le sur la table, mais ne le mets pas ici
sentences.cue: Put it on the table, but don't put it here
sentences.literal: Put-it on the table, but not it put not here

words.note: Whole: the order and its object joined by a hyphen. That le is L3-M5's object pronoun — it, not L1-M1's article the — and it sits behind the verb only while the order is positive.

sentences.trap: The hyphen is not decoration and it does not survive the negative. Mets-le becomes Ne le mets pas: the pronoun moves in front of the verb and the hyphen disappears with the move.
sentences.sound: meh-LUH sewr la TABL, meh nuh luh meh pah ee-SEE. Behind the verb that le is said LUH, full and stressed; in front of it, it almost vanishes.

variations.display: Mets-le ici
variations.cue: Put it here
variations.changed: one order, one pronoun, nothing else

variations.display: Ne le mets pas sur la table
variations.cue: Don't put it on the table
variations.changed: the negative alone, with the pronoun back in front and no hyphen

mistake.why: The hyphen goes when the order turns negative, and the pronoun goes in front of the verb: Ne le mets pas ici.

sentences.usage: The half-sentence a learner has to build twice before it stops feeling backwards.
sentences.mnemonic: Positive pushes the pronoun back; negative pulls it forward.

sentences.display: Il suffit de tourner la clé pour ouvrir la porte
sentences.cue: You just have to turn the key to open the door
sentences.literal: It suffices of to-turn the key for to-open the door

words.cue: you just have to · all it takes is
words.note: One frozen key, three words. The il names nobody, exactly like the il of il faut, and whatever follows de stays an infinitive.

sentences.trap: There is no you in it. French says il suffit de and English has to supply a person — you just have to — so the two sentences never line up word for word.
sentences.sound: eel sew-FEE duh toor-NAY la KLAY poor oo-VREER la PORT. The t of suffit is silent and the de runs straight on.

variations.display: Il suffit de tourner la clé
variations.cue: You just have to turn the key
variations.changed: the purpose drops off and the frame stands alone

variations.display: Pour ouvrir la porte, il suffit de tourner la clé
variations.cue: To open the door, you just have to turn the key
variations.changed: the purpose leads and the frame follows it

mistake.display: Il suffit de tournes la clé
mistake.why: de hands the next verb its infinitive: il suffit de tourner. Nothing after it is ever conjugated.

sentences.usage: How you tell somebody a machine is simpler than it looks.
sentences.mnemonic: il suffit de, then an infinitive, always.

sentences.display: Continue tout droit, ensuite tourne à droite
sentences.cue: Keep going straight on, then turn right
sentences.literal: Continue all straight, then turn to right

words.note: Imperative of continuer, an -er verb: no -s. One French word for what English needs two of, and the final e is silent.
Imperative of tourner, L2-M4's verb: tu tournes gives Tourne. L2-M4 named this form and refused to write it, because it was speaking to a stranger.

sentences.trap: Continue is spelled like the English word and is not read like it: three syllables, stress at the end, and a silent e that English pronounces.
sentences.sound: kon-tee-NEW too DRWAH, ahn-SWEET TOORN a DRWAT.

variations.display: Continue tout droit
variations.cue: Keep going straight on
variations.changed: the second step comes off

variations.display: Tourne à droite, ensuite continue tout droit
variations.cue: Turn right, then keep going straight on
variations.changed: the two steps swap places

mistake.why: continuer is an -er verb, so its tu imperative has no -s: Continue.

sentences.usage: Directions given to somebody you are on tu terms with — a friend, a child, a brother.

sentences.display: Écoute-moi bien et n'oublie pas la page trois
sentences.cue: Listen to me carefully and don't forget page three
sentences.literal: Listen-me well and not-forget not the page three

words.note: Whole: Écoute plus its object on a hyphen. Behind a positive order me becomes moi, L2-M1's stressed form, and écouter takes its object with no a in front of it.
ne elides to n' before a vowel and is still fully there. oublie is the -er imperative of oublier, and the pas lands after it.
Feminine: la page. The number follows it with no preposition at all — la page trois, never la page de trois.

sentences.trap: Listen to me is three words in English and the to is not one of them in French. écouter carries its object directly, so écoute à moi is wrong twice over: wrong preposition, wrong pronoun.
sentences.sound: ay-koot-MWAH bee-AN ay noo-BLEE pah la pahzh TRWAH. The n' of n'oublie is heard, and it is the only thing carrying the negative into the ear.

variations.display: Écoute-moi bien
variations.cue: Listen to me carefully
variations.changed: the second half comes off

variations.display: N'oublie pas la page trois
variations.cue: Don't forget page three
variations.changed: the negative order alone, with its n' still written

mistake.why: Behind a positive order the pronoun takes its stressed shape: Écoute-moi.

sentences.usage: A teacher to a class, a parent to a child — the register the vous imperative of L2-M4 could never reach.
sentences.mnemonic: Behind the verb, me grows into moi.

sentences.display: Vas-y, appelle le bureau et demande la recette
sentences.cue: Go on, call the office and ask for the recipe
sentences.literal: Go-there, call the office and ask the recipe

words.note: The one place aller's imperative takes its -s back: Va on its own, Vas-y with the y behind it. Literally go there, and used where English says go on.
Imperative of appeler, an -er verb, so no -s — but the l doubles before the silent ending: nous appelons keeps one, tu appelles and Appelle take two.

sentences.trap: demander is ask FOR, and it takes no preposition: demande la recette. A demande pour la recette is English showing straight through the French.
sentences.sound: va-ZEE, a-PEL luh bew-ROH ay duh-MAHND la ruh-SET. The s of vas-y is heard as a z, which is the whole reason it is written.

variations.display: Vas-y, appelle le bureau
variations.cue: Go on, call the office
variations.changed: the second order comes off

variations.display: Appelle le bureau et demande la recette
variations.cue: Call the office and ask for the recipe
variations.changed: vas-y drops, and the pair of orders stands on its own

mistake.why: aller's imperative takes its -s back before y, so the two can be said at all: Vas-y.

sentences.usage: The push you give somebody who is hesitating, and the commonest thing said just before a phone call.
